newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan trys to lure rebels to peace accord - papers.
newsitem.headline: Sudan trys to lure rebels to peace accord - papers.

text.p: Sudanese newspapers on Wednesday quoted officials as saying contacts with rebel factions were in progress to try to persuade them to join in a peace agreement.
In April, the government and six rebel groups signed an accord that does not include the mainstream Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang.

"Extensive contacts are being made these days... with the sons of the state (of South Kordofan), who are under the SPLA-Jebel Nuba faction, including (its leader) Yousif Kuwa," the government daily Al-Anbaa quoted State Governor Habib Makhtoum as saying.

The private Alwan newspaper quoted the acting governor of the southern Upper Nile state, Abu Bakr Deng, as saying the state government was making contact with Lam Akol's SPLA-United to try to include them in the process.
"Dialogue is going on with this group for it to join the peace process," Deng said. "The government has never closed the door to dialogue."
Khartoum hopes the accord will end more than 10 years of war. Parliament endorsed it earlier this month but it has yet to be ratified by President Omar Hassan al-Bashir.
The agreement says there will be a four-year transitional period during which southern Sudanese are meant to decide whether to secede.
